EXACT-2026-01 applies across the existing three jurisdictions; it is not a fourth Fundamental Theorem. Adoption adds no discharged guarantee. The two scoped QLV1 admissions and the original three broader pending obligations retain their identities and status; additional proof and enforcement duties remain separate. Issue #311 tracks the interpretation’s integration.

Change and impact review

A language feature, semantic breaking change, or change to the acceptance or trusted boundary must record its constitutional impact before admission. The record must cover:

  • each of QS, PR and RS, identifying an applicable binding interpretation or a pending interpretation question and explaining the affected scope;
  • changes to normative definitions, accepted representations, trusted assumptions or semantic primitives;
  • applicable ledger entries, current acceptance/artifact bindings and any required semantic transport;
  • existing proof coverage, new proof or evidence duties, and remaining gaps;
  • constitutional edition impact, separately from release compatibility and source/artifact migration.

This is the change-review process tracked in Issue #140. A routine change already covered by existing interpretations need not obtain a new individual Guardian ruling or invent a new proof. It must identify that coverage. Wording, test refactors and implementation changes with no constitutional effect may record that conclusion with its reason. New constitutional cases or disputes require the Office’s interpretation; the author’s impact assessment is not a substitute for that ruling.

Proposed semantic primitives must additionally justify why ordinary checked source, elaboration, a verified transformation or target lowering is insufficient, and state the effects on the trusted boundary and all three obligations. Performance or popularity alone is insufficient. A backend intrinsic that implements an existing meaning does not thereby acquire a new primitive meaning. The primitive admission and replacement policy provides the checklist, derived-code presumption, rejected performance-only example, edition-aware migration and inventory obligations for Issue #154. It preserves the current ban on project axioms and unchecked acceptance paths. New independent semantic meanings still require actual human specification review; a new constitutional case requires the responsible human Guardian judgment. Ordinary preserving implementation choices need no invented adoption event. This chapter admits no new primitive or trusted assumption.

Conflicts and corrections

  • If a formalization omits an applicable protected case, repair and prove the obligation. The omission creates no constitutional exemption.
  • If required proof or evidence fails, repair the implementation or proof, or withhold the affected acceptance or certification. A Guardian ruling cannot waive the failure.
  • If a later interpretation conflicts with a discharged guarantee, preserve or strengthen the guarantee through the recorded correction process. Neither renaming nor narrowing the formal boundary can remove its protected scope.
  • If the Reference and implementation disagree, resolve the specification or conformance defect under the higher requirements. Passing examples and tests do not redefine the language. An informative guide cannot settle the conflict.
  • If ratified constitutional text must change, follow Article III’s edition amendment process and Article IV’s non-weakening rule, except for a valid strictly pre-v1 Article IX rectification. That exception requires an explicit reasoned human authorization, repairs an already adopted principle and expires permanently at v1.0.0.

Adding a new Fundamental-Theorem jurisdiction requires constitutional amendment and an edition transition. Applying QS, PR or RS to a new case, or proving a helper lemma, does not add a jurisdiction. New jurisdictions must justify their distinct enduring purpose, relation to existing obligations, assumptions and current proof coverage; see Issue #138. An edition increment cannot authorize weakening an existing protected guarantee.

Editions, releases and compatibility

An edition identifies the constitutional regime, not a grammar generation, source dialect or compiler version. A release/formalization state identifies the current implementation, accepted language and formal realization within that regime. Syntax, type-system and CLI changes belong to release versioning and its published compatibility and migration policy. The unified 0.3.0 language therefore remains in constitutional edition 2026.

Source trees explicitly declare the constitutional edition through schema-2 Qargo.toml, in [qrate].edition. Updating the compiler does not implicitly change that selection. Edition identity alone does not identify an executable checker version, a grammar, a complete acceptance predicate or a proof of all three obligations.

Record the constitutional edition and complete product release as separate coordinates: for this development snapshot, (2026, 0.3.0-beta). Qargo manifest schema 2, the QLV3 envelope and native-result schema 3 are distinct format revisions; none selects another constitutional edition. The native decision binds the requested edition, compiled product version, canonical mode and checked scope to the actual checked subject. Those fields do not authenticate the native executable or establish source/runtime preservation.

The release records retain edition, product and format identities alongside the actual commit, artifacts, checker/proof scope and ledger identity. Version synchronization does not migrate an edition or constitute ratification. Release validation, source compatibility and a constitutional amendment retain their separate requirements.

Constitutional continuity, source compatibility and continued implementation support are separate promises. Reducing the accepted language does not by itself weaken a safety implication, but may violate the release compatibility policy. Retiring a parser does not erase historical ledger guarantees. Any historical case accepted through a current migration remains subject to its applicable guarantees and justified connection to the current artifact.

Policy, constitutional harness and execution

Policy as Theorem. Constitution as Harness. Compiler as Executor.

This is Qleisli’s top-level architecture principle. It has three parts, and this chapter gives a section to each. The principle is subordinate to the authority hierarchy, the ratified Constitution and the recorded human interpretations. It defines no mathematical interpretation and no discharged guarantee.

The qrate and external-artifact boundary distinguishes five kinds of role: semantic, evidence, observational, realization and organizational. It states explicitly the current package limitations and edition-binding limitations.

Policy as Theorem

A policy that affects constitutional acceptance must become a formal proposition, or an evidence obligation, whose discharge can be checked independently. An implementation convention, a theorem name, a test or a successful compilation cannot supply that authority.

The Constitution Guardian, a natural human, determines the binding constitutional interpretation for a defined case. The interpretation says what must be proved, which scope and premises apply, and how the requirement relates to existing guarantees. Lean, or the designated independent proof checker, establishes that the resulting proposition is derivable under its actual definitions and recorded assumptions. Human interpretation and mathematical verification are separate judgments. Ordinary maintainers select language and implementation designs within those requirements. Routine covered maintenance needs no further interpretation.

QS, PR and quantitative RS are three permanent, distinct proof obligations. Their binding meanings come from the adopted interpretations. This chapter freezes no predicate and no theorem type. Evidence must connect the claimed property to the actual production acceptance and to the current accepted artifact. A source claim additionally requires its source-preservation link. A realization claim requires correspondence to the actual output. A resource claim requires the specified bound for the actual behavior or realization. A proof about a convenient unused predicate cannot replace those links.

The initial interpretations and scoped guarantees record current coverage. Only ordinary QLV1 root ownership and classical scope have been admitted as scoped guarantees. Broader QS, PR, quantitative RS and the EXACT supplement retain pending duties. Passing a compiler check does not discharge them. The Fundamental Theorems do not themselves prove any of these components correct: the Rust frontend, the native compiler, the decoder, the simulator or the exporter. Each claimed correspondence retains its own obligations and assumptions.

Constitution as Harness

The Constitution fixes four things: permanent obligations, human interpretive authority, recording procedures and continuity. Discharged guarantees accumulate for their recorded scopes and premises. A future syntax, provider, backend, representation, release or tool cannot escape an applicable obligation by renaming its acceptance path or by moving it. A changed representation requires the appropriate checked semantic transport. Old proof files alone are insufficient. Edition identifies this constitutional regime. Syntax compatibility and release compatibility are separate matters.

The harness must reach executable boundaries. Prefer making a prohibited operation unrepresentable, untypable, unverifiable or explicitly rejected. External prompts, coding conventions and author identity cannot be the only protection for an accepted guarantee. Identity, continuity, production coverage and required evidence belong in mechanical enforcement, with their actual limitations exposed. The CI checks implement parts of that harness. Constitutional CI and the release gate have unfinished requirements. History links to them.

Pre-v1 proof maturity permits the truthful disclosure of incomplete coverage. It never permits any of these: withdrawing an admitted guarantee, treating a failed check as successful, or advertising an unproved scope as constitutionally certified.

Compiler as Executor

The compiler executes policy; it does not create policy.

The language and its ecosystem are the executable surface of these constraints. These steps apply the authorized contracts: parsing, name resolution, the preparation of types, effects and ownership, the generation of evidence, and lowering. Native Lean checking supplies each fresh semantic accepted handle under the constitutional theorem boundary. Rust proposals, authored source and external IR are all subject to the applicable independent checks. When native checking is absent, incompatible or fails, the result is a rejection. Nothing falls back to another acceptance authority.

BoundaryEnforcement and user-visible meaning
Ordinary values and quantum ownersT and Q<T> are distinct. Preparation and measurement are explicit. Expected typing cannot insert either.
Ownership, axes and phaseEvery owner, including zero-width owners, is accounted for. Width is not interface identity. Permutation and nontrivial phase are explicit.
Effects and capabilitiesA body cannot downgrade Observe to Unitary. Unitarity alone supplies no inverse or control API. Declared evidence and access obligations must be checked.
Workspace and temporary accessWhen they are admitted, clean/dirty features and access features must enforce their adopted all-input/reference contracts. Planned syntax is not such evidence, and neither is a successful known-input test.
Source and external artifactsAn external provider or schema cannot manufacture semantic authority. An independent check of valid output IR does not alone prove that the IR corresponds to its source or to its target.
Qrate, module and toolchainExplicit identities and closed substitutions govern checking. Ambient names or a plausible provider are not evidence.

The type model, primitive boundary and realization contracts state the rules and the profile limits. This table does not implement the unfinished access, workspace, realization or surface proposals.

Crossing a protected boundary must fail closed and explain the violated rule. A safe expressible alternative may be suggested when one exists. Unsupported constructs, missing evidence and failed native checks must never silently become any of these: weaker semantics, a hidden discard or reset, implicit physical coercions, or unchecked backend acceptance. A diagnostic may explain a proof gap. It cannot waive the gap.

Diagnostics and inspectable recovery

Diagnostics are constitutional pedagogy: they make an enforced boundary visible to humans and coding agents. A useful rejection identifies the boundary and the likely classical assumption. It also identifies the canonical Qleisli construct, where one is available, and a recovery that preserves the contract. For example, when an explicit Op provider is missing, the rejection names the unresolved binding. It does not search for a convenient implementation. A quantum wildcard must not silently consume an owner. Text and JSON describe the same failure and source location. The diagnostic reference lists categories, recovery guidance, and conformance cases.

An unfamiliar derived stdlib abstraction should have an inspectable recovery path. The path is to read its signature, inspect the ordinary checked .qli implementation, and then follow its calls to language rules and specified primitives. Derived code must undergo the same applicable checking as user code. Source location, first-party status and documentation generation confer no semantic authority. Language primitives require their canonical contracts and independent checks. Reading an implementation cannot reconstruct or authorize a different meaning. The primitive inventory and current limitations separate this policy from the source cutover and from the open proof obligations and profile obligations of that cutover.

Three Qleisli tools are planned: QLT, the Qleisli Testsuite; QDB, the Qleisli Debugger; and QCP, the Qleisli Circuit Profiler. They and qargo, qlidoc and other tools are subordinate interfaces. They may expose programs, facts, diagnostics or evidence. They cannot adopt interpretations, waive proof, create a parallel acceptance path or weaken accepted meaning. Their implementation is later work. This chapter installs none of those tools. mdBook is the separate build environment for the documentation. It creates no language authority and no API-introspection authority.

Inference and explicit discovery

This section sorts the concepts of the language and its tools into two categories. The categories say how an author who meets a concept for the first time finds its meaning.

For human authors and coding agents, zero-prior inferable means that an author can recover the intended semantic role without knowing Qleisli-specific names. Familiar spelling or similar-looking code alone is insufficient. Explicitly discoverable means that a canonical introduction exposes the role and its contract. The author does not have to guess the name of the construct first. These are categories for documentation and design. They are not claims about the measured success rate of an LLM, and they are not permission to infer quantum meaning.

ConceptCategory and recovery path
Ordinary modules, imports, tuples and bindersInferable where their ordinary meaning survives. The source/type Reference and located diagnostics identify the exact syntax and predictable classical mistakes.
Quantum owners, effects, access capabilities and MeaningExplicit discovery through the type, Rust and functional boundary chapters. Classical familiarity cannot supply their quantum obligations.
Derived stdlib abstractionsExplicit discovery through the signature and mathematical contract, then ordinary .qli source under stdlib/src/ and its callees. Source inspection does not itself prove the contract.
Language primitives and external providersExplicit discovery through the primitive and production boundaries. Reading derived source cannot reconstruct or grant their semantic authority.
First-party ecosystem tools, including QLT, QDB and QCPExplicit discovery through qleisli --help, then qleisli help ecosystem. Each tool’s role and current availability are stated there. These are Qleisli-native discovery targets.

The help path works without a project and without a native checker. It issues no accepted handle. Planned tools are unavailable for execution. Predictable classical mistakes need correction paths that are deterministic and located and that preserve owners, phase and evidence. Semantic ambiguity must reject. Naming must avoid misleading pseudo-analogues and semantic false friends. Every future first-party addition to the language or to the ecosystem must declare its category, its intended semantic role and its canonical recovery or discovery path. This implements the documentation boundary for inference and discovery within the Reference.

Required review of future designs

This section is a checklist for the author of a design document. Every major design document for the language or for its tooling must identify how it preserves:

  1. the applicable adopted interpretation, scope, premises and existing guarantees;
  2. formal obligations, actual acceptance/artifact bindings, checked evidence and open proof gaps;
  3. authorized source rules, lowering, ownership/effects, exact phase/axes and fail-closed behavior;
  4. diagnostic recovery, inspectable derived source and explicit tool discovery;
  5. the distinction between human interpretation, formal verification and execution.

Use the existing constitutional impact procedure and the GitHub decision record. An unresolved constitutional case that existing interpretations do not cover requires the concrete human judgment. Ordinary implementation within existing interpretations is maintenance. No design document gains constitutional authority by completing this checklist.

Shared production boundary and premises

The initial scope is the currently admitted finite/raw and sized/hierarchical production paths of edition 2026, including their source, Rust, CLI, Python and foreign-format callers. A future feature remains subject to all applicable obligations; omission from today’s examples or proofs creates no exemption. The scope and evidence must be updated when the admitted language grows.

Decision #276 places production acceptance in the Mathlib-free native Lean checker. For ordinary QIRF, the concrete chain includes the original artifact and optional independent request bytes in the QLV1 packet, QleisliKernel.Protocol.Validity.check, and QleisliKernel.Qirf.Validity.inspect. On the Rust side, interchange::native::Kernel obtains the fresh decision and authorizes private accepted handles associated with those bytes. The hierarchy has its own native structural/request checks and freshly checked finite obligations. The ordinary QIRF theorem alone does not cover that entire hierarchy.

For each claimed guarantee, its release record must identify the real entry points, admitted profile, original inputs, requested contract when present, checked representation and current artifact consumed by execution or export. It must account for the selected checker and its compatibility/provenance assumptions. A theorem about an unused predicate, a subset chosen only to make the theorem easier, or a producer’s success receipt cannot stand for production acceptance. A structural hierarchy derivation cannot silently stand for the missing analytic meaning of its complete accepted operator.

The policy in TRUSTBOUNDARY.md remains in force, as described in the production authority chapter: reference meanings require human specification review; frontend output, synthesis search and other proposals require independent validation. Native compilation/runtime, decoding, source lowering, Rust re-materialization, execution and emitted-output correspondence must retain their actual assumptions and proof gaps. Moving code into Lean or obtaining an accepted handle does not discharge all those links. Source acceptance must be connected to the source’s specified meaning before source preservation is claimed.

New sealed semantics require the admission review proposed in Issue #154: exact meaning, reference behavior, owners/effects, phase/coordinates, target/workspace and resource obligations, and why ordinary checked source or a verified transformation is insufficient. Popularity or performance alone is insufficient. An implementation intrinsic must implement an existing meaning or undergo that review. No interpretation here authorizes project axioms, unsafe/partial executable definitions or runtime replacements. A reviewed semantic assumption is not a permission to add a Lean project axiom.

Adoption identifies obligations and their current gaps. It does not confer full pre-v1 certification on existing accepted paths, change the acceptance implementation or enable external schemas. Article VIII requires truthful scope-specific claims throughout this work. The full supported-profile Soundness/specification/review milestone remains v0.5.0; the complete three- obligation conformance requirement remains the separate v1 milestone.

1. Interpretation QS-2026-01 — Meaning of accepted programs

Scope: the current production program/evidence acceptance boundary above, with the particular guarantee stated separately for an ordinary root, an independently requested finite contract, a hierarchy, or a source-level claim. These are coverage distinctions within QS, not alternative acceptance authorities.

Obligation: the actual accepted program must satisfy its declared typing, ownership, effect and semantic contracts, interpreted independently of the checker and evidence producer. An independently supplied requested meaning must bind the accepted implementation, its dependency evidence and its full interface. An ordinary acceptance without such a request must not be advertised as proof of an arbitrary external functional specification.

The required properties and premises are:

  • Preserve logical owners, including zero-width owners, complete tuple/basis shape, finite sizes and the ordered mapping from interface axes to the interpreted operator. Equal width alone does not identify an interface.
  • Preserve linear use, global identity freshness, lexical classical scope, simultaneous branch-phi inputs and the complete live caller frame. Separate owners do not imply separable quantum states. Measurement consumes its logical owner; discard is explicit and has its declared semantics.
  • Interpret pure operations as the specified exact maps, including exact phase before taking a density-operator interpretation. Matching probabilities or equality up to global phase cannot replace an exact operation contract, especially when coherent control can expose relative phase. Unitarity alone supplies neither an inverse API nor controlled access.
  • Interpret observing programs by their unnormalized, outcome-indexed completely positive maps, acting correctly with arbitrary external references. Account for hidden measurement, reset and discard histories and the declared classical output/coarse-graining map. Trace preservation is a property of the complete admitted instrument; checking individual sampled results or renormalized branches does not establish it.
  • Require exact semantic discharge of clean workspace, and the distinct restoration obligation for dirty workspace, as described below.
  • Preserve these properties through the actual admitted composition and transformations. Any source or runtime claim needs its corresponding preservation link, beyond acceptance of a proposed IR object.

For clean workspace A, suppose the program denotes a finite-dimensional CPTP map E_p from A ⊗ R_in to A ⊗ R_out, with A initially in |0><0|. For an observing program, R_out includes its declared classical outcome register: the premise concerns the complete instrument, not a normalized selected branch. Define the reduced live-system channel by Phi(rho) = Tr_A(E_p(|0><0|_A ⊗ rho)). Exact return of the workspace marginal to |0><0| for every density operator on R_in is equivalent to the following separation condition for every finite external reference E and every joint density operator rho on R_in ⊗ E:

(E_p ⊗ id_E)(|0><0|_A ⊗ rho)
  = |0><0|_A ⊗ (Phi ⊗ id_E)(rho)

The equivalence requires the all-input, exact, fixed-pure-state premises; the two formulations are not independent extra obligations. Observing branches must retain their unnormalized probabilities in the corresponding instrument formulation. Dirty workspace instead requires restoration of its unknown state and reference correlations according to its declared identity contract. A known-input test or workspace marginal alone is insufficient for dirty return. This follows the proposed distinction in Issue #157. Approximate marginal cleanliness does not imply separation with the same error parameter; this packet admits no approximate cleanup or epsilon contract.

Candidate evidence and gaps: Qleisli.NativeValidity.check_sound binds success of the actual Lean QLV1 checker definition to Qleisli.Qirf.Validity.VerifiedMeaning. Its ordinary root carries structural postconditions, independent linear ResourceSafe and classical ScopeSafe; an optional finite request additionally carries the stated original-instrument finite contract. Qleisli.Qirf.Validity.requested_reference_laws supplies the stated finite-reference inverse laws for that requested contract. These are useful candidate evidence, not a complete ordinary-root EffectSound/CPTP or source/runtime theorem. Qleisli.NativeHierarchy.checkLeaves_semantics and Qleisli.NativeHierarchy.conditional_derives connect fresh native finite leaves to their structural derivations; general analytic LeafMeaning-to-Operator closure remains a separate duty. Their existing scope, reference definitions, assumptions and relation to each public acceptance path still need review before any ledger discharge is recorded.

2. Interpretation PR-2026-01 — Accepted target realizations

Scope: each target realization for which Qleisli claims executable or exported implementation of an accepted semantic program, including its actual emitted circuit/artifact, target/profile and checked evidence. A semantic accepted handle alone is not target-realization certification.

Obligation: every realization admitted by the production realization gate must implement the already accepted meaning under its stated target and workspace contract. The record must bind the current accepted program/request, target, emitted artifact and evidence to that gate. Checking a different internal circuit or retaining a producer’s claim is insufficient.

Required premises include the declared primitive gate actions and device assumptions, input/output encoding and coordinate order, effects and classical outcomes, admitted synthesis workspace, initialization/restoration, and the exact equality contract. Workspace may exceed the semantic program’s original wires; semantic unitarity does not prove same-wire synthesis. Clean and dirty workspace obey the QS distinctions above and remain counted while live under RS.

Exact operation contracts retain their phase. A projective equality claim would require an explicit permitted contract and a proof that its intended contexts respect that quotient; it cannot discharge an existing exact or coherently controlled contract by silently discarding phase. No target gate set, coefficient ring, projective relaxation or approximate synthesis facility is admitted merely by adopting this interpretation.

This is the forward correspondence duty proposed in Issue #281. It does not require that every matrix in an independently specified mathematical domain have a realization, or that Qleisli implement a complete synthesis algorithm for it. Target/profile existence and synthesis-completeness theorems may be proved separately and used to produce evidence. Independently supplied realizations are admissible only through the same checked correspondence gate. Missing synthesis is an unsupported target realization; it is not permission for a fallback that certifies unchecked output. Inverse and controlled capabilities remain separate obligations.

Candidate evidence and gaps: finite circuit/contract, hierarchy and exact algebra theorems may supply components of correspondence. They do not by themselves connect every current exporter, target lowering or synthesized artifact to the requested meaning. This packet identifies no discharged production-wide PR theorem and does not treat successful QIR emission, simulation, native acceptance or physical-device assumptions as that theorem. Each concrete target claim must expose the missing links or provide their checked proof before that scope is certified.

3. Interpretation RS-2026-01 — Quantitative resource accountability

Scope: finite, statically computable bounds for the resource semantics applicable to the current accepted program, its admitted specialization/family and, where claimed, its current target realization. The resource contract must state input/size premises, counted quantities, target capacity and scheduling assumptions, and all permitted branches.

Obligation: actual accepted behavior and actual admitted transformations must respect independently checked finite resource bounds. Composition, lowering, optimization, synthesis and emission must preserve the bound contract or produce and validate a justified replacement bound for the resulting artifact. An estimate about a different circuit cannot certify the emitted artifact.

The current resource model must explicitly select its measures: for example, peak live width, clean/dirty/backend workspace, gate or non-Clifford counts, measurement and feed-forward counts, and depth under a specified schedule. Alternative classical outcomes require the declared safe bound over permitted execution paths; a mean from sampled runs does not establish that bound. Workspace returned clean still counts for its live interval. Correct semantics or a valid realization alone does not prove compliance with a target capacity.

A closed finite specialization may admit concrete checked accounting. An admitted family needs a justified bound function over its stated parameters, without treating finitely many tested instances as its proof. New runtime control, opaque providers or target-dependent synthesis must activate the corresponding bound obligations before claims of certified resource coverage. Untrusted external annotations require checking and composition; they cannot grant their own resource authority.

This applies the proposed quantitative jurisdiction in Issue #280. Linear ownership, no implicit discard and clean/dirty restoration belong primarily to QS. ResourceSafe in the current ownership proofs does not establish this RS claim. Checker work counters, input limits and host timeouts constrain the verification implementation; they do not constitute a program/target resource bound unless a separately specified correspondence establishes such a claim.

Candidate evidence and gaps: finite accounting structures and ownership proofs can support later constructions, but this packet identifies no completed production-wide quantitative RS discharge. Required resource semantics, certificate rules and preservation links must be specified and checked against current production artifacts. The existing Resource Safety target remains distinct from clean discharge. Later compatible features may strengthen its proof burden without creating a fourth obligation or escaping edition 2026. This interpretation grants no permission for approximation or other future syntax.

Evidence, continuity and the recorded human decision

The working directions in Issues #135, #136 and #139 inform this packet. Their text and the cited Lean declarations are not binding interpretations merely because they exist. This packet’s binding force comes from the recorded human adoption. Current theorem statements may evolve; mathematical meaning requires reviewed reference definitions independent of the checker or proof decomposition. The statement-isolation work in Issue #306 remains a v0.5.0 obligation and must preserve the link to actual production acceptance.

Each adopted interpretation is recorded first as a binding pending obligation, with its exact reviewed text, human decision, scope and premises. Existing proof coverage must then be matched to the interpreted requirement and independently verified before a separate discharge record can enter the ledger. A successful audit, an ordinary helper lemma or approval of this packet alone does not create a discharged guarantee.

For every later discharge, bind the protected property, fragment, premises, semantic definitions, proof/evidence and current acceptance/artifacts. Later releases must preserve applicable ledger guarantees against their own real acceptance machinery, with justified embeddings and semantic transport where representations differ. An implication between two old closed theorems is insufficient. New capabilities outside old fragments remain subject to the current obligations. Acceptance continuity and source support also retain their separate published compatibility duties.

Current production verification boundary

The production verification boundary is the set of entry paths that reach the native checker, together with what each check establishes. The native checker is the Lean executable that lean-kernel/ builds. A mode is one dispatch argument of the native checker, such as --runtime-root-check. An entry path is a Rust API or a CLI command that submits bytes to a mode.

Read this chapter to find out what a successful check proves and what it leaves open. For each mode, the chapter states four things: the request that the mode reads, the rules that the native checker applies, the Lean theorems that bind the check, and the obligations that no theorem discharges. The section on a mode lists the theorems under the label “Proof scope” and the open obligations under the label “Not established”.

The chapter is subordinate to three documents: the authority hierarchy, the adopted single-verifier decision that History cites, and repository TRUSTBOUNDARY.md. It does not discharge a constitutional obligation or widen an existing theorem. Source paths identify files in the Qleisli repository.

Production acceptance has one implementation, the native checker. Rust does the work around the check and never accepts a program itself.

Rules:

  • Rust generates proposals, and it selects and invokes the compatible checker. It retains the checked bytes, which are immutable. It also decodes views, reports diagnostics and executes simulations.
  • A missing, incompatible or failing native checker rejects. No other verifier takes its place: the retired Rust verifier and the dual-acceptance fallback are absent.
  • Invoking Lean and granting a semantic accepted handle are different things. Not every public function does either. Public operations that confer no acceptance lists the operations that produce no acceptance. One of them invokes Lean all the same: QIRF export has the native checker inspect its output. That check establishes portable validity. It is neither a fresh execution acceptance nor a translation theorem.

Constitutional theorem boundary

The diagram below places the native check between the proposal of an artifact and the three constitutional obligations QS, PR and RS. It applies to the implementation that this chapter describes, under the adopted interpretations and the single-verifier decision.

Source or external artifact, with its requested contract when present
    |
    v
Elaboration or adaptation proposes artifact and evidence bytes
    |
    v
------------ independent production acceptance boundary ------------
Native Lean gate checks the actual bytes, profile and applicable evidence
    |
    v
Accepted judgment binds the decoded artifact, contract and evidence
    |
    +--> QS  Independent semantics of the accepted artifact
    +--> PR  Checked correspondence of an admitted target artifact
    +--> RS  Checked bounds on accepted behavior and admitted realization

The accepted judgment of a mode is the success of its Lean check on the submitted bytes. Entrypoints and actual checked representations identifies the judgment and the checked representation of each mode. Two scoped guarantees are admitted. They concern ownership and classical scope of the original decoded ordinary root.

Under the adopted interpretations, the three obligations concern these subjects:

ObligationSubject
QSThe declared typing, ownership, effect and exact semantic contracts of the actual accepted object
PRForward correspondence from that meaning to the actual admitted target artifact, under its target and workspace premises
RSFinite, checked bounds for the accepted behavior and the applicable realization, under the stated resource model

Their broader proof obligations and the strict exactness obligations are pending.

Rules:

  • Elaboration must preserve the specified source meaning for every claimed source scope. Its evidence links the original source and dependency contracts to the checked artifact, including its owners, ordered axes, effects and exact phase.
  • A successful check of an artifact establishes the properties of that artifact that the check covers. It does not establish that the artifact corresponds to its source. A preservation theorem or independent validation must establish the source correspondence separately.
  • The same rule applies to an adapter that claims to preserve a foreign input, and to a backend that claims preservation in the output it emits.
  • Source syntax that a later change adds may elaborate under the same edition whenever it preserves the adopted contracts.
  • A checked representation that replaces another must carry the applicable current guarantees with it, through justified semantic transport.
  • Every frontend and backend that claims constitutional acceptance must use the applicable native gate and its current evidence.
  • Missing evidence or a failed check rejects the claimed scope.

Implementation note. lean-kernel/Main.lean dispatches the native modes, each of which has an explicit version. The engineering comparisons are among them and are mechanically separate. lean-kernel/Cli/NativeContext.lean invokes the pure dispatcher Protocol.NativeContext.run and its single reply projection. It checks the original QLV3 edition and the compiled product, and then applies the existing gate of the mode. The strict version-3 reply binds that same context. The older IO adapters are unused and await retirement after replacement conformance coverage. They are not fallback entry points.

lean/Qleisli/Qirf.lean defines the graph denotation that these bridge files use. It contains none of the theorems that this chapter cites by name.

Ordinary QIRF root requests

The mode --qirf-native checks an ordinary QIRF root. Checking or compiling a source, a project or a qrate reaches this mode. The first row of the entry-path table lists its entry paths and its bytes. The bytes are a QLV3 envelope. The envelope holds the original QLV1 packet, with its optional independent request. When the caller requests execution, it also holds the retained execution view.

Rules:

  • The accepted judgment is the success of QleisliKernel.Protocol.ExecutionView.Native.ordinary on the QLV3 payload at its requested scope. The checker reaches that function through Protocol.NativeContext.run.
  • Execution requires one more check: a comparison of the retained view against the view that Lean decodes.

Proof scope:

  • ordinary_original binds the accepted judgment to Protocol.Validity.Acceptance for the original QLV1 packet. That witness identifies the decoded Qirf.Artifact, the order and the optional independent request. It also identifies the success of Qirf.Validity.inspect on those exact values.
  • Qleisli.NativeValidity.check_sound binds success to VerifiedMeaning.
  • check_scopeSafe covers classical scope.

Not established:

  • Full ordinary EffectSound/CPTP is a separate obligation.
  • Preservation by source translation and preservation by foreign translation are separate obligations.
  • Preservation in emitted output and preservation at runtime are separate obligations.

Native contract requests

A caller uses the mode --qirf-contract when it needs a fact about a QIRF root beyond ordinary validity: an encoded equation, an exact matrix, a control sector or an observing instrument. The mode reads the original QIRF root and, beside it, a qleisli.native-contract request of version 1. It decodes the request strictly. The field kind selects one of six request kinds:

kindFieldsSection
encodedformat, version, kind, contractEncoded and square leaf
leafformat, version, kind, signature, input, output, matrixEncoded and square leaf
pure-leafformat, version, kind, domain, codomain, input, output, matrixRectangular pure leaf
controlformat, version, kind, signature, axesControl sector
control-ownersformat, version, kind, signatures, axesControl sector
instrumentformat, version, kind, actual_signature, expected_signature, identity, expected_artifactObserving instrument

Rules:

  • The inner QLV1 format is the same for every kind. An external call requires the QLV3 envelope and its scope.
  • The control kind changes neither the inner QLV1 format nor the contracts of the encoded and leaf requests.

Proof scope:

  • The native-contract bridge is specific to Protocol.NativeContract.check. It does not inherit the theorem for the ordinary Protocol.Validity.check root.
  • Its Acceptance witness retains what the check read and decoded: the original QLV1 body and request bytes, the UTF-8/JSON decoding, the artifact and order, the requested signature, the ordered ports and the exact matrix or encoded contract. It retains them with continuous work states. These facts are necessary for success. They are not a converse characterization of every parser constraint.
  • Protocol.NativeContract.check_acceptance binds the original bytes, the decoded request and the actual checking states.
  • tests/fixtures/constitution_v030/native-contract-bridge/ preserves the unchanged executable prefix, the printed theorem and predicate types, the axiom sets and a validation record.

Not established:

  • The identity and proof checks of that fixture admit no guarantee and do not close S05.
  • They establish no claim about the source or the compiler, a deployed binary, Rust rematerialization, the target or the runtime, or quantitative Resource Safety.

Encoded and square-leaf requests

A request of kind encoded states an encoded equation for the root. A request of kind leaf states a signature, ordered ports and an exact square matrix for it. The entry-path table gives the entry paths and the checked bytes of the kinds encoded and leaf.

Rules:

  • The square kind: "leaf" protocol keeps its two-sided unitary conditions. It is available beside the rectangular kind.

Proof scope:

  • Qleisli.NativeContract.check_encoded_sound and encoded_meaning connect success to three things: the BodyMeaning of the original root, the exact Basis interface and the requested encoded equation. Through EncodedMeaning, the encoded branch retains that BodyMeaning, the complete Basis interface and the checked encoded equation.
  • Wrapper.circuitMatrix_entries proves that the coefficients of the actual wrapper equal those of the original matrix.
  • encoded_reference extends the equation to any reference amplitude function.
  • Qleisli.NativeContract.check_sound and leaf_meaning compose the native acceptance of the bytes to the instrument meaning of the original body. They cover the bounded closed unitary fragment, the exact requested matrix, the signature and the ordered ports. The output port is tied to an actual verification.
  • leaf_reference_laws extends both whole-space inverse laws to every finite reference. The leaf conclusion retains complex phase. Its laws for an arbitrary finite reference require no premise of separability or normalization.

Not established:

  • For the kind encoded, these claims are separate: source and compiler, compiled I/O, runtime and export, clean release and quantitative resources. The theorems are not ledger admissions.
  • For the kind leaf, source and runtime claims are separate. Broader claims about effects and clean release are separate too.
  • Both kinds give bounded results about the original root. These results do not establish correspondence with the source, with a deployed binary or with host execution.

Rectangular pure-leaf requests

A request of kind pure-leaf states that a unary pure function equals an exact matrix. The input type and the output type are independent, so the matrix can be rectangular. The mode --qirf-contract accepts qleisli.native-contract version 1 with kind: "pure-leaf". Its complete fields are format, version, kind, domain, codomain, input, output and matrix.

Rules:

  • Both types use exact QIRF basis trees. The ports retain token, ordered wires and bit shape.
  • The native checker rejects an unknown field, an unknown version and a producer acceptance flag.
  • The interface of the original QIRF root describes a unary pure function with independent input and output types. The structural check of that interface requires four things: a Unitary or Isometry effect, no classical ports, one input and one actual live output owner, and the corresponding input and output widths.
  • The reader of the literal original body finds the output owner. The input width does not stand for the output width.
  • Ordinary validity alone does not establish an external matrix equation.
  • PureLeaf.check freshly checks the original dependency graph and body. It binds both exact type trees and both ordered ports. It reconstructs every input column, and it checks exact equality to the requested matrix and V†V = I.
  • Reconstruction retains the original effect checks, complete classical branches and hidden observation histories. Measurement, reset and discard cannot be relabeled pure or erased from the equation.
  • Zero-width owners, exact phase and axis order are part of the obligation.
  • Both endpoint dimensions keep the six-bit dense bound and the shared exact-work accounting. The kind adds no unbounded matrix API.
  • Every receipt requires fresh native acceptance, including a receipt that uses previously checked dependency data.

Implementation note. CheckedPureLeaf is a receipt that only private code can construct. It covers the immutable bytes of the original artifact and of the request. On the Rust side, boundary construction and matrix serialization validate only the shape of untrusted data.

Implementation note. The ordinary frontend retains SourcePureEquation sidecars on its accepted entry. A sidecar holds an implementation leaf and a reference leaf, each independently checked. It also holds their exact matching domain, codomain and matrix, the resolved names and the original source text. Constructor lowering rechecks actual renamed Raw fragments against the derived matrix. Selected Raw lowering retains its original Meaning requests and checks actual instruction intervals. The refined finite-leaf path of the hierarchy is square and refuses rectangular Meaning obligations.

Proof scope:

  • pure_leaf_meaning binds the fresh check of the graph and the root to the original body and the exact Gram identity.
  • pure_leaf_reference preserves inner products for arbitrary joint reference amplitudes.

Not established:

  • The check grants neither inverse nor control access. It supplies no source or runtime correspondence, no target realization and no quantitative resource evidence.
  • Source snapshots provide provenance. Neither sidecar is a general proof of source preservation, a functional specification of an arbitrary whole entry or a constitutional guarantee.

Original-artifact control-sector requests

A control-sector check asks whether an action keeps the computational-basis sectors of the requested axes apart. The rules below state the exact condition. Each source ctrl call carries such a check as an obligation. The mode --qirf-contract accepts two kinds that request a control-sector check of an original artifact:

RequestComplete field setContent
kind: "control"format, version, kind, signature and axessignature is the exact QIRF basis tree. axes is an ordered list of distinct physical bit positions in that interface.
kind = "control-owners"format, version, kind, signatures and axessignatures is the requested basis forest of an original call with several ordered quantum ports.

Rules:

  • The native checker rejects a control request with an extra field. A proposed matrix is such a field, and so is a producer success flag.
  • A control-owners request carries exactly its five fields. It accepts neither a proposed matrix nor a success receipt.
  • Lean checks the original graph, the root and the dependency evidence, and it checks that the input and output interfaces are identical. It reconstructs the actual action and checks that the action is unitary on the whole space. It then requires every matrix entry between different requested computational-basis sectors to be exactly zero.
  • The six-bit finite reconstruction limit and continuous work accounting apply.
  • An empty axis list is meaningful for a zero-width logical owner. It does not erase ownership or nontrivial phase.
  • The internal Qirf.ControlAccess.checkOwners component checks an original call with several ordered quantum ports. It constructs no wrapper that packs them into a single port. The requested basis forest must match the widths and positions of the original input owners and of the live returned owners, including zero-width owners.
  • Raw bit widths do not establish source type trees. The requested forest requires binding to the original checked source.

Rules for source ctrl calls:

  • The Finite project path binds the control-owners request before it updates source bindings. It binds the request to each interval of an actual emitted control call, to the original ordered owner ports and basis forest, and to the returned tokens. It checks nested calls and unused concrete declarations. The complete final artifact also requires ordinary native acceptance.
  • Selected source projection retains the original ordered access roles, together with the source identities and positions of the call. This includes public ctrl occurrences. Elaboration checks the exact owner shape and actual effect. It neither grants sector authority nor rewrites the role to excl.
  • Checker-free Raw lowering and hierarchical lowering reject retained control roles.
  • Native-checked Selected Raw lowering independently checks the selected root and every retained concrete body that bears a control. It then replays its actual decoded calls with fresh sector requests. Final consumption repeats native acceptance and source replay. Retaining a role or an earlier success is not acceptance authority.
  • The common judgment records each original control call as a pending sector obligation. Native-checked Selected Raw lowering requires every original obligation to have a concrete interval in each retained specialization of its declaration. A program with an absent interval is unsupported. One specialization cannot cover the missing call of another.
  • Unused original declarations, unselected branches, empty loops and zero-count providers cannot erase the obligation or its location. Retained zero-count provider bodies are checked before root emission.
  • Control replay refuses when it has no native checker.
  • Symbolic inverse or controlled replay refuses retained control roles. Its transformed trace does not supply the original call intervals that the native bridge requires.
  • Zero-count and unused-provider obligations must be covered before selected transport can be admitted. Empty output does not waive them.

Implementation note. The internal Raw replay bridge can discharge a retained control obligation with the checker of the accepted original artifact. It selects the actual instruction interval that replay consumes, its input and returned tokens and its ordered source basis forest. It then submits a fresh control-owners request. It takes no call body, matrix or success receipt from a producer.

Work is shared across these decisions within the exact-work ceiling. The checked Raw entry shares this budget across all body and root decisions. It refuses an increased ceiling, exhaustion or an unavailable checker. Regression tests use original public control source graphs as well as private graph mutations.

Proof scope:

  • Protocol.NativeContract.ControlAcceptance and check_acceptance retain the original body and request bytes, the exact decoded signature and axes, and the actual checker execution.
  • Qleisli.NativeContract.control_meaning connects the same action to four things: the BodyMeaning of the original root, its exact interface, the sector condition and the inverse laws.
  • control_reference proves projector commutation on arbitrary joint complex amplitudes with any external reference. Phase kickback and entanglement are permitted. The result does not assert that the reduced control state is unchanged, and it does not assert separability.
  • checked_owners_meaning and checked_owners_action_project bind the actual root, its dependencies and the full complex action to the sector law.
  • ControlOwnersAcceptance retains the decoded ordered forest and coordinates, the original packet bytes and the actual checking execution.
  • control_owners_meaning and control_owners_reference extend the original-body result and the arbitrary-reference result to the control-owners request.

Not established:

  • The control request alone does not enable source ctrl calls.
  • These are separate obligations: original source places, the artifact identity that is specific to a call, aliasing, access lifetimes, lowering and execution correspondence, and quantitative resource and scheduling claims.
  • The two kinds introduce no native mode, external schema admission or constitutional guarantee.
  • Neither an annotation nor native unitarity alone supplies control-sector evidence.
  • Host source lowering and interval extraction are not a Lean source-preservation theorem.
  • AST-to-step preservation, Rust decoding and interval extraction are separate obligations. The Raw replay bridge is a host bridge, not a Lean source-preservation theorem.

Original-artifact observing instrument requests

A request of kind instrument compares two observing artifacts, the actual one and an expected one. The check succeeds only when the two are equal as instruments. The mode --qirf-contract accepts kind = "instrument" in qleisli.native-contract version 1. Its exact fields are format, version, kind and the four below:

FieldContent
actual_signature, expected_signatureEach signature has exactly input and result. input is the QIRF basis tree. result is a complete result tree.
identityExactly implementation, specification and sources. Each source has exactly path and text.
expected_artifactThe original expected QIRF JSON as a UTF-8 string

The complete result tree uses these exact objects:

ResultFields
Ordinary Unit or Bit{"tag":"unit"} or {"tag":"bit"}
Ordinary Bits{"tag":"bits","width":N}, with a u32 natural width, including zero
Quantum owner{"tag":"quantum","basis":B}, with the complete QIRF basis tree
Pair{"tag":"pair","left":L,"right":R}
Tuple of at least three values{"tag":"tuple","fields":[...]}

Rules:

  • The native checker rejects a request that supplies a matrix, a receipt or a success flag. It also rejects a request with a missing field or an extra field.
  • The actual QIRF is the original QLV1 body. The checker freshly checks both complete graphs, both selected roots and the dependency evidence.
  • The kind changes neither the QLV1 framing, the QIRF representation nor the other request kinds.
  • The signatures must agree as entire trees, including Unit, Bits<0>, zero-width quantum owners and product nodes.
  • The ordered quantum owners and the classical projection must match the original roots.
  • Source consumers select this contract by the Observe effects that callers see.
  • The native profile requires original artifacts that genuinely observe. A pure body can carry a conservative Observe bound. That bound neither rewrites the Raw classification of the body nor authorizes a fallback to a pure contract.
  • Unsupported concrete pairs refuse, including unused ones.
  • The native profile has one quantum input and no runtime classical inputs.
  • Signatures are requested type data. Native widths alone do not reconstruct the full types of the source or prove their preservation.
  • The equality has no tolerance.
LimitValue
Sources in identity128, with the name and path bounds
Aggregate identity bytes1 MiB
Depth of a result tree64
Nodes of a result tree4,096
Dense reconstructionSix bits, with the shared work and JSON limits
Transport16 MiB

Implementation note. The private Rust instrument handle retains both original accepted artifacts, the complete signature, the source identity and the fresh paired native decision. Both concrete apply_contract adapters execute only the implementation. They check its actual emitted interval again against the immutable reference. Each private call sidecar retains the original ports, instructions, result IDs and source span. The enclosing root has its separate ordinary acceptance. Unused original closed obligations are also checked.

Selected Raw preparation independently replays the original implementation. It then checks the consumed instruction interval, the actual input owner and the ordered result through a fresh native equation. The retained proposal keeps the original pairs and private call sidecars. Later source validation checks again with the checker of the accepted artifact. Dependencies, unused declarations and zero-count children keep their original obligations. Hierarchy lowering and checker-free emission reject this overload.

Proof scope:

  • Protocol.NativeContract.InstrumentAcceptance retains the original decoded request, the original expected text, the fresh expected graph and continuous checking states.
  • Qleisli.NativeContract.instrument_meaning, check_sound and check_encoded_sound connect success to the instrument meanings of both original bodies, to complete Kraus sums and to untruncated dimensions. They also connect it to identical unnormalized public outcome maps on any joint matrix with a finite external reference.
  • The independent reference in Qleisli.Semantics.InstrumentEquality sums all hidden histories. Neither their count nor their labels are public outcomes.

Not established:

  • The check grants no observing Meaning, coherent control or adjoint access. Pure Meaning retains its exact phase rule.
  • The sidecars do not change QIRF. They do not set request_checked or source_meaning_verified of a request-free root to true. Inspection of a whole root without a request reports no independent requested meaning.
  • Source preservation, decoder preservation, preservation by native compilation and runtime, and emitted-artifact preservation are separate obligations.
  • The lemmas admit no constitutional guarantee.

Finite nominal carrier requests

The internal mode --carrier-pure-check checks a pure body that maps one forest of nominal owners to another. It checks the body against an independent exact logical matrix.

ItemValue
Formatqleisli.carrier-request
Version1, strict
Profilefinite-carrier-pure-v1
Fieldsformat, version, profile, attached, required and logical

Rules:

  • Both interfaces retain complete ordered owner forests and public effects.
  • A nominal atom retains the identities of its original module, declaration and source, and it retains its member order. Its logical cardinality and its physical width do not affect this.
  • Singleton enums and empty records are distinct from Unit and Bits<0>.
  • Protocol.Carrier.check reconstructs the original declarations, import paths and existing field Nat helpers before it checks the actual graph and root.
  • The core freshly checks three things: the Gram equations of both canonical codes, the Gram equation of the logical map and physical * E_in = E_out * logical.
  • Logical dimensions govern the Unitary label. A larger physical unitary does not justify a logical Unitary claim.
  • Observation, reset and discard cannot be hidden as pure.
  • Extra source rows require exact nominal origins after source checking. Ordinary checking keeps its own source-use rule. Uncovered helper rows and import-only rows refuse.
  • The source, matrix and work limits apply.

Implementation note. The explicit source adapter uses the common judgment, the selected Builder and the Raw emitter. It requires an independent logical request and replays retained source steps against the checked body. Its sealed CheckedSourceCarrier retains that source graph and always reports source_meaning_verified() == false. Descriptors and source preparation grant no acceptance.

Proof scope:

  • CheckedCarrier.run_binding binds the execution-only QLV3 packet and the actual QDV1 comparison of the graph, both interfaces and the logical matrix. The binding retains the original packet and the exact QDV1 comparison.
  • Its Binding.root_safe follows the actual checked root to the independent ownership and classical-scope properties.
  • The core postcondition binds the actual body/code equations and the Gram equations.
  • The source adapter adds a replay of the retained steps. It adds no ordinary runtime, no inverse or control access and no AST-preservation theorem.

Not established:

  • Neither this result nor the private native carrier holder converts to an ordinary execution handle or grants inverse or control access.
  • The runtime route for closed ordinary results is the separate mode of Ordinary input/result requests.
  • This component does not supply general nominal functions, quantum owners, full qmatch or original AST-to-step preservation.
  • These component results admit no guarantee and do not widen the two existing ledger scopes.

Ordinary input/result requests

The internal mode --ordinary-root-check checks one original declaration whose parameters and result are ordinary values. It checks the declared parameters and the result over the complete input domain of the declaration, that is, for every value of the parameters.

ItemValue
Formatqleisli.ordinary-root-request
Version2
Profilefinite-ordinary-root-v2
Fieldsformat, version, profile, selection, module, declaration, parameters, input_storage, input_rows, basis, storage and public_effect

The field selection names one of three selections:

SelectionDeclaration that it denotes
ProjectExactly closed main::main, including a private ordinary main
ExportedAn original public declaration
InternalAn original private non-entry declaration. Checking does not export its name.

Rules:

  • The fields are strict. The native checker rejects a Version1 request, an unknown field and an unknown profile, and it tries no fallback.
  • Original parameter and result types must be ordinary finite types. This mode does not support quantum ports.
  • A selection that names a public main explicitly uses the exported rule. The restrictions on a project main are separate.
  • The basis retains the complete nominal prefix representation. Storage separately retains Unit, Bit, Bits, pair, tuple, enum origin and SSA coordinates, and record origin and ordered named children. Zero-width nodes cannot be discarded.
  • The checker freshly reads the original ordered parameter forest and the declared result, and compares them with the request. Argument count and zero-width arguments stay explicit.
  • Five original checks run first: the Raw root, dependency, ownership, effect and scope checks. The complete exact reconstruction of the instrument follows them.
  • Lean independently enumerates the entire canonical parameter domain, with the first argument on the low coordinates. It requires exact equality with the proposed input_rows.
  • Lean checks typed input storage for every row. It then interprets every actual hidden history, including zero-probability histories, with the independent ordinary-value relation.
  • Flattened input and output SSA maps must equal the original Raw lists.
  • An invalid enum code, a changed nominal identity, a reordered field or axis, or a hidden Observe under a pure label refuses.
  • A declared public Observe bound is retained even for a pure implementation.
  • The six-bit instrument limit and the carrier and work limits apply.

Rules for source rows:

  • Source rows require the actual selected original, exact checked nominal origins, or actual original type-resolution paths from the selected parameter and result types and recursive record fields.
  • The ordinary and mixed runtime gates use the original body reader when signature and graph evidence leave source rows uncovered. This binds body-only type paths, including paths through called helpers, before the shared Raw root check.
  • The shared independent resolver retains its exact query, original lookup bytes, visibility and import and reexport edges.
  • An arbitrary row or a validated unused Nat helper cannot supply type-path coverage.
  • Projection and both coverage scans are precharged within the work limit.
  • Coverage binds source relevance to the checked artifact.

Rules for execution and transport:

  • Closed simulation and sampling inspect the retained parameter forest. They reject a nonempty forest even when every parameter has zero width. Unit, Bits<0> and empty records require an actual invocation even when the Raw input lists are empty. A nullary typed result is closed.
  • The run_closed/sample_closed APIs reject any nonclosed root. Checking parameters adds no unchecked arbitrary-input execution API.
  • Untyped rechecking and portable export refuse until the complete typed artifact transport exists.
  • Untrusted portable nominal emission refuses until its complete typed request is transported.
  • This mode checks the declared result and the histories. Text and JSON reports distinguish that check from an independent external specification of an algorithm.

Implementation note. Nongeneric public selected functions use this gate through the common original-source compiler. The gate covers small quantum temporaries, which it checks over every hidden history. Interfaces are ordinary in this mode. Mixed quantum interfaces use Mixed runtime root requests. Selection retains the exact original instantiation, the complete checked host bindings and the accepted request. Ordinary source callers use the common original-body lowering.

Implementation note. The source wrapper discharges dormant function pairs through the same contract gate as project checking. It prepares the original Meaning and body dependencies that global obligations visit.

Implementation note. The private ordinary proposal decoder of Rust accounts for the path and text of every proposed source under the aggregate identity limit. It then defers relevance to this native gate and returns no accepted handle. Other decoding routes keep their unused-row refusal. The ordinary execution view compares every retained original source byte before a fresh accepted handle is bound. The private accepted program retains the same typed request, the complete checked input rows and the graph.

Proof scope:

  • Protocol.OrdinaryRoot.check_binding retains the original packet, the fresh artifact and request reads and the actual root check.
  • The execution-only QDV comparison and the native dispatcher retain this binding through CheckedOrdinaryRoot and run_typed_ordinary_binding.

Not established:

  • This mode does not check a declaration with static parameters. A selected root with Basis/Nat actuals uses the mode of Mixed runtime root requests, whose emitter also closes ordinary Basis/Nat dependencies.
  • Full qmatch and nominal finite-table consumers are separate work.
  • Source-to-Raw correspondence is a separate obligation.
  • No preservation theorem follows for the source body, the decoder, the native compiler, the simulator or the target. No external schema, inverse or control capability or guarantee follows.

Mixed runtime root requests

The internal mode --runtime-root-check checks a root whose interface mixes ordinary values and quantum owners.

ItemValue
Formatqleisli.runtime-root-request
Version2, strict
Profilefinite-runtime-root-v2
Fieldsformat, version, profile, selection, module, declaration, parameters, input_storage, input_rows, result, storage, public_effect, static_bases and static_naturals

Rules:

  • The native checker rejects a Version1 request.
  • The full prefixes of the parameters and of the result preserve each Q boundary, nominal declaration, ordinary tuple and zero-width owner.
  • Storage binds actual ordinary SSA values and ordered quantum ports.
  • A producer writes these descriptions. The original runtime signature check and the shared Raw root checks are independent of them.
  • The request must name complete Basis and Nat actuals, including those of unused formals. The checker rechecks the original premises and nominal declarations before it instantiates the actual header tokens.
  • QLV3/QDV retains these actuals even when they do not change the runtime graph.
  • For every independently enumerated ordinary input, RuntimeFamily reconstructs all hidden maps. It checks ordinary results even on zero-probability histories. It checks the exact code-space equations of the input and of the output, and their complete logical Gram sum.
  • Physical padding may not leak into a logical result.
  • Observation stays Observe, and a Unitary label requires equal logical dimensions.
  • The six-bit dense component limit and the work limits apply.
  • QLV3/QDV compares the complete request and the actual retained graph.
  • The native decision is execution-only. Inspection and caller scopes refuse.
  • Original parameters prevent closed execution even at zero physical width.
  • Portable export cannot erase the metadata of AcceptedProgram::runtime_result.

Rules for the choice of request:

  • The compiler selects the request before native root checking. It never retries a failed native decision.
  • The selected entry uses this mode when every selection has its own whole-circuit check and the original operation closure does not require version 5.
  • Three things use the bounded request of Version 5: source-body requests instead: nominal source gates, wider selection sectors and the transport of the original operation closure. That section also specifies the checks of coherent basis lifts, with_computed, access receipts, qfor and Meaning applications.
  • A small nominal named-arm qmatch function also submits its complete actual callee fragment to the version-4 mode of Qmatch source requests, before whole-root runtime acceptance.

Implementation note. Kernel::check_runtime_root and fresh check_program rechecking bind the same objects to the native decision. AcceptedProgram::runtime_result exposes read-only metadata. The common project and selected emitter uses this gate for mixed runtime interfaces. It retains actual input storage before call expansion, and complete output types and owners afterward.

Implementation note. Selected roots with Basis/Nat actuals use the same emitter and gate, including unused nominal actuals and closed observing bodies. Their complete original source judgment is repeated, and actual trees are rebound to its original interface. Ordinary Basis/Nat dependencies use the same original call plans and bounded closure. Concrete nominal arguments use the type(T) form. Forwarded formals retain their original binder identities. Nominal fields keep their declaration scope. Complete closed siblings are checked even when a different actual is unresolved. Unused nominal actuals also require typed checking when the global dormant pass materializes a closed dependency.

Implementation note. Selected built-in qmatch and its ordinary callers also use this emitter. Named operation arms require their original provider bodies to pass the finite evidence gates. The actual emitted circuit also passes the separate six-bit encoded equation.

Proof scope:

  • RuntimeRoot.check_binding, CheckedRuntimeRoot.run_binding and NativeContext.run_typed_runtime_binding connect actual reads and comparisons.
  • The root safety theorem reuses the original Raw gate. It enlarges neither of the two guarantees that humans admitted.

Not established:

  • This mode does not enable operation-formal closure. The version-5 request transports the original operation closure.
  • This mode checks a coherent selection only through its whole-circuit check. The version-5 request checks wider selection sectors within its bounds.
  • Exact computation witnesses are separate from complex denotation, source-body preservation and numerical runtime correspondence.
  • Independent host-expression visibility and source/body preservation are separate obligations.
  • No external schema, inverse or control capability, guarantee admission or broader QS/PR/RS/EXACT discharge follows from this mode.

Qmatch source requests

A qleisli.qmatch-request asks the checker to compare the parts of a source function with their literal Raw intervals. Two modes read such a request. Each accepts one version of the request:

VersionModeProfileSubject
4--qmatch-source-checkfinite-source-qmatch-context-v4The named-arm component: Version 4
5--qmatch-source-v5-checkOne of four profilesThe original source body: Version 5

The full qmatch profile is the source contract of qmatch at its full size, with twelve joined bits and 64 labels. Neither version validates the full qmatch profile.

The production compile path dispatches both versions, and a successful reply of either mode has the claim accepted. A version-4 success binds the private component QmatchChecked. A version-5 success binds an accepted program.

Version 4: named-arm component requests

The internal mode --qmatch-source-check checks the named-arm component: the qmatch selections with named arms in one complete structural quantum function, together with every literal Raw interval of that function.

ItemValue
Formatqleisli.qmatch-request
Version4
Profilefinite-source-qmatch-context-v4
ScopeExecution only
Fields and QDV recordThe request and QDV schema specifies them.

Rules:

  • The request and the QDV record bind every site to one fresh graph. For each site they bind its complete typed interfaces, its original source byte occurrence, its literal Raw interval and its actual evidence and control indices.
  • Every original selection appears in order. The intervals exhaust the complete call without gaps or overlaps. Each interval retains its actual owner frame and passes its own exact equations.
  • Original source reads determine the canonical labels, types, owners, public effects and source rows. Actual receipt inputs and dependency snapshots bind the named arm bodies.
  • The pure finite, Raw, QIRF and nominal gates check the exact sector equations of main, U and CU.
  • The request binds the selected pair separately, with the selector before the target. It retains additional arguments, zero-width owners and the outer public effect.
  • Nominal enum and record targets, including empty records, retain their full original types with enum or built-in ordinal selectors. Their physical arm entries and controls are untrusted proposals. The mode binds the full target type, the actual body and the code equations. It issues no provider capability.
  • The ordinary source-root wrapper keeps its original main-only roots and its empty extra source-query extension.
  • The check spends from the shared exact-work ceiling.

Rules for the ordered Raw frame:

  • The frame requires a complete structural source return. Checked renaming, ordinary tuple moves and the final expression retain the original logical owner identities, basis trees and returned order.
  • Unknown suffix expressions, hidden observation or discard, and missing or duplicated owners refuse.
  • A legal source return that changes owner order requires a matching Raw output mapping. Equal types or empty wire lists do not justify reusing the unswapped Raw subject.
  • The original Raw operations transport an independently derived logical owner tree. Explicit joins retain ordered children. Splits recover those children. Owner-moving operations retain their complete source roles.
  • The actual output-token order must match the original source return. Reversing two empty Raw ports cannot pass for a canonical source return. A zero-width permutation that matches between source and Raw is accepted.
  • Physical widths constrain a split without identifying a logical owner. A producer supplies no role table and no cached tree.

Implementation note. Kernel::check_qmatch_source invokes the mode. The Rust walker describes the actual retained graph and the circuit and matrix caches. The same allocations enter QmatchChecked only after two matches succeed: the exact QDV match, and the native match of product, edition, mode, scope and request.

Implementation note. A small nominal named-arm qmatch function submits its complete actual callee fragment to this mode before whole-root runtime acceptance. The fragment retains its original complete quantum argument and result order, its structural body and its named-arm evidence. Suspended caller owners stay in the complete outer Raw state. The bounded source adapter retains the actual complete call and restores the frame of the suspended caller. It does not synthesize a replacement source function or expose a raw conversion of QmatchChecked. The component uses an internal canonical owner frame. That frame is not a language restriction.

Implementation note. Shared conformance cases cover three- and four-label nominal selectors on two physical bits with a distinct zero-width Unit target, reordered written arms and exact relative phases. The three-state code leaves its padding label outside the logical interface. Literal retained-view expectations include the four dyadic coordinates of an eighth-root phase. Phase, control-polarity and evidence faults must reach the equation gate. Original nominal, arm and owner substitutions reach the request gate, and stale compared output reaches QDV refusal.

Proof scope:

  • The structural execution proof recovers the historical snapshot of each entry from the same successful graph run. It preserves every dependency that the entry references in the final root. It transports the original IR execution with identical exact operators, hidden histories, failures and unspent work. It covers references in both branches even when the condition is constant. Unrelated slots may differ. The common context result retains this execution property in its ordered original arm-binding relation. The proof does not prove the meaning or the lowering of the original source body.
  • The original-arm continuation is not wired into source or transport admission. It reuses the actual checked signature and body through the common source traversal.
