It then checks the IR of the realized entry under those same final dependencies. Supported bodies inherit the explicit scope of the common reader. Selections require their recursive arm equations. The continuation enables no native request, handle or broader source preservation claim.
  • Generic success bindings retain the original Raw ownership and classical-scope properties without enlarging either human-admitted guarantee.

Not established:

  • No public conversion yields an ordinary AcceptedProgram, an inverse capability or a controlled capability.
  • Data constructors, request encoding and source headers alone supply no source-function theorem.
  • The component checks alone supply neither ordinary source execution nor the full qmatch profile. The bounded compiler adapter also requires separate whole-root runtime acceptance.
  • These are pending: general source expressions and call frames, other valid mappings, constructed, static and generic arms, and the full qmatch profile.
  • The structural-return check does not establish general source or arm lowering, and it does not expose ordinary source execution.
  • Splitting an opaque source owner, allocation and release, and a changed representation each need their own checked source rule or refinement. The structural component does not establish every valid Raw mapping or complete source preservation.
  • Fresh native conformance, canonical proof maintenance and full CI are required. Original source-body lowering, decoder, walker and native compilation, runtime and target preservation, and broader QS/PR/RS/EXACT duties are separate.

Version 5: source-body requests

The mode --qmatch-source-v5-check checks the source body of one original invocation. The source body consists of the coherent selections, basis lifts, computed intervals, access calls and Meaning applications of the invocation. The mode checks each of them against its literal Raw interval. The request also carries the runtime-root request of the same root.

Kernel::check_qmatch_source_v5 submits the request that the compiler selects. The accepted program records the checked profile, which CLI success reports names.

ItemValue
Formatqleisli.qmatch-request
Version5
ProfileOne of the four profiles below
ScopeExecution only
ProfileBody that earns it
finite-source-qmatch-context-v5A body with checked selections
finite-source-meaning-context-v5A standalone Meaning application. The native traversal binds an actual application interval and discharges the original Meaning duties of the selected invocation. Other roots retain their pending positions for separate checks.
finite-source-basis-context-v5A body with no selection or Meaning context and with an actual checked basis lift or computed interval. The check discharges the original duties of the selected invocation and retains pending positions that belong to other invocations.
finite-source-access-context-v5A standalone original access body. The native replay finds an access receipt in the actual checked steps of the selected invocation, its named calls or its branches.

Rules:

  • The checker checks the original nominal declarations and import paths that constructors and field projections use in the body, even when the types do not occur in the selected interface.
  • The check spends from the shared exact-work ceiling.

Rules for coherent basis lifts:

  • Selected bodies and project bodies may include coherent basis lifts with nominal values.
  • The native checker independently derives the logical table from the original finite expression and the pure helper bodies. It checks the dependencies of every ordinary match arm, and binds the canonical rows to the actual Raw lift interval.

Rules for with_computed:

  • This mode also checks a protected two-argument with_computed with an original nominal predicate. Lean evaluates the total classical predicate on the exact logical codes and requires zero in the padding rows. It checks the original one-Bit use body against both exact diagonal entries of the literal Raw use. The same interval retains the original data owner and its spectators.
  • Selected runtime functions and projects that use this mode support circuit synthesis for first-order Boolean predicates on built-in basis inputs. Lean checks the ordered controls and both compute passes against the original predicate. It then checks the protected use on both auxiliary values. This path checks the predicate and both circuits in their structural representation.
  • The synthesis path charges work for the source expression, intermediate clause products, literal circuit fields and owner-frame checks. The charge includes intermediate conjunction products, even when the final circuit is smaller. The path uses one private scratch bit and the work and interface limits.
  • For example, a two-bit increment modulo four can use the checked carry predicate word[0] and word[1] as a controlled phase between Hadamards on the high bit, followed by a low-bit flip.
  • The literal take_bit and put_bit intervals retain the original register coordinates and arbitrary reference amplitudes.
  • A finite transform such as a specialized adjoint, control or power selects the checked finite representation when it prepares its original body.
  • The three-argument certified form binds the original use body and the logical supplier independently to their literal circuits, on the exact data and auxiliary codes.
  • Explicit pair splits and joins retain their written owner order and the exact logical axes, including padding in the product code.
  • The native cleanup equation covers the complete physical domain.

Rules for access receipts:

  • An access receipt binds the written arguments and their roles to the actual callee, the ordered quantum ports, the returns and the Raw interval.
  • Ordinary Unit arguments keep their original positions in the call.
  • A routed exclusive named call also checks its original Bit arguments, its ordinary branch, its parked owners and the complete extraction and reinsertion.
  • The checker verifies complete coverage of the selected invocation. It retains the pending positions of the other invocations.
  • The separate provider proof of a transform does not supply this receipt.
  • The access profile is part of the compared QDV1 execution view.

Rules for inline arms and qfor:

  • For qif and qmatch, a written inline arm submits its original arm index, its source positions and its literal Raw body. Lean replays the original block in the isolated target frame. It compares the resulting exact action with the controlled implementation and with the Raw sector of the caller. Mixed named and inline arms use that same sector check.
  • For a supported original qfor with closed bounds, Lean follows the written iteration order. It checks that the literal Raw intervals cover the loop body contiguously. It checks the carried register and the surviving owner frames at the boundaries, including zero-width owners.

Rules for Meaning applications:

  • A selected coherent arm can use an original classical Meaning helper with nominal intermediate values when the ports of the Meaning are supported built-in types. Lean checks the helper against the original canonical inputs and compares the exact Meaning with the applied arm. Standalone applications can use the same equation check.
  • Standalone applications also check endomorphic permutation_by and phase_by Meanings with finite nominal ports through the same native path. Lean checks the original provider body, the exact logical action on its canonical codes and the literal application.
  • A composed Meaning can pass through a nominal intermediate type. Tensor Meanings retain the ordered logical axes of their nominal and built-in components.
  • A reused Meaning evaluation requires the same original declarations, reference occurrences, exact ports, ordered graph edges and dependency rows in both source queries.
  • A rectangular application through a named call retains the written checked_op at its supplying argument, even when the callee leaves the argument unused. A rectangular application checks the distinct input and output codes against the actual Raw interval and preserves the spectator frame.
  • A Meaning declared on an operation formal checks the exact supplied argument, including unused actuals. The original header duty and any checked_op written at the call site each retain their own source occurrence.

Rules for operation arguments and Meaning duties:

  • The internal common-body duty continuation authenticates every original operation argument in scalar-free Op calls against the complete ordered header keys. This includes unused siblings. A forwarded formal retains its original mixed-header ordinal.
  • The supplying assertion and the enclosing arm retain separate original queue positions, source tokens, provider occurrences and exact Meaning equations under the same final native root.
  • An authenticated interior formal path may locate a supplying assertion inside a constructed argument. The continuation requires exactly one original requested node with fully bound children. It checks every other local provider and ordered descendant.
  • Unknown providers, further missing requests and ambiguous supplying occurrences are residual.
  • The complete original call and the mixed-header keys of the supplying root are checked again. An enclosing equation cannot replace the inner equation.

Implementation note. For a basis lift, the producer evaluates only the original logical rows and completes unused physical inputs injectively. For predicate synthesis, the compiler emits controlled XOR steps from constants, input bits, literal Bits<n> coordinates, Boolean operations, tuple bindings and supported helper calls.

Implementation note. One retained development regression, for two-qubit general composition, has an explicit exception for preparation work. History cites it. The regression runs two steps separately: source preparation, which accepts nothing, and the unchanged whole-body action under the normal budget. It reports aggregate work and independently checks all sixteen exact I4 entries. It issues no handle and is not one bounded production acceptance. The public 20,000,000 ceiling and its entry guard are unchanged.

Proof scope of version 5

The theorems below concern a successful version-5 check and the original body that it reads. Their namespaces begin with Runtime, or are RawFiniteRows, and are defined in lean/Qleisli/.

Several theorems concern three adjacent original named calls: the pre call, the middle call, which holds the selection, and the post call. The proofs name the middle call “choose”. A three-call root is an original root whose Raw events are the slices of these three calls and one final reorder.

Coherent selection:

  • RuntimeSelectionAction.caller_action covers a Bit selector and a Bit target. It relates the literal Raw events to both indexed logical arm matrices on the complete returned owner code. It covers a single quantumIf and the compiler’s join, apply_unitary, split sequence. The original logical selector and target determine which matrix and row act. This holds also when the selected wires are reversed or separated by spectators.
  • RuntimeSelectionGram.logical_gram proves that inner products are preserved for arbitrary joint caller and reference amplitudes, under the same two arm receipts.
  • RuntimeSelectionGram.checked_selection obtains both receipts and the canonical order [0, 1] from the source layout reads and from the logical matrix comparison that the native selection node retains.
  • RuntimeMultiwayAction.checked_selection covers any checked finite selector with a Bit target, under the same literal interval and owner-code premises. Each encoded selector label determines one original arm. On valid encoded inputs, the physical output agrees with that arm at every output row, including zero amplitude on padding labels. The same arm receipts preserve the logical inner product with an arbitrary external reference.

Predicate synthesis:

  • Lean proves the exact work that the predicate compiler debits and that both circuit comparisons debit.

The three-call root and the source flow:

  • RuntimeNamedThreeRoot.Whole.instrument_decomposition factors the independent instrument meaning of the original root into the three actual event slices and its final output permutation. It retains complete intermediate history families, including hidden and zero-weight outcomes, without normalization or reassociation of the bounded evaluator.
  • RuntimeNamedCodeTransport concerns the checked original return map from a child to its caller. It proves that the map preserves complete basis trees, ports, the independent sparse-code interpretation and ordered axes in the same caller frame.
  • These two results are laws about return transport and about the Raw instrument. They do not compose the different source-level encodings and logical actions.
  • RuntimeNamedSourceFlow.original_body derives the named-boundary state chain from the actual common body loop and its retained successful traversal. It retains the real initial owner reorder and the final source-return read. The proof follows both fresh and planned event traversal, including selected static continuations, with the original continuous work counter. It factors the recursive iteration without changing its guards, reads or charges.
  • original_three connects the actual pre, middle and post calls through their complete source states. Those states include ordered bindings, full bases, ports and issuance history. Equal physical widths and assumed code equations are not premises.
  • The state-flow invariant is administrative. Other step kinds receive no named-boundary assertion from it. It establishes no composition of whole-source code, of logical action or of observing history.
  • RuntimeNamedChildRuns.original_body strengthens the same loop proof with the actual recursive run of every named child on its original callee and native block. The retained input read binds the original parameter owners of the callee to the selected ports and original input owners of the caller. The recursive call uses the same checked visible ordinary SSA. It starts with the work that the input read leaves. Its exact result determines the stored child steps, the returned history and the ordinary state.
  • The same stored step list carries an OrdinaryRun from the actual initial SSA state to the actual returned SSA state. It retains the tables and measurement keys across gaps, observations, named calls and conditionals. Pure steps preserve both. Its literal partition covers the complete original Raw operation list in order.
  • RuntimeLiteralBody.original_body_trace reads each exact interval through the independent observing reader. Adjacent steps share the full Raw boundary state, and their events concatenate to the trace of the original body.
  • RuntimeLiteralBody.original_body_execution splits a successful independent run at those exact boundaries. Each step runs on every incoming history and keeps the result order of the interpreter. The execution induction follows the same source-owner and SSA chains. A proved local invariant therefore applies to every returned history of the original body.
  • The weaker state-flow law is derived from this single strengthened proof. original_child_runs supplies those computations for the actual pre, middle and post view. Other step constructors receive no child-provenance assertion here. The proof establishes no whole-source code or action composition and no observing-history composition.

The pre and post calls:

  • The state-flow proof aligns actual primitive nodes with both their complete source input history and their checked output history. Its primitive handler, operation and selection case proofs share the existing loop. Other step constructors acquire no state or code assertion.
  • RuntimeNamedPrimitiveInputs.original_pre_post_inputs derives the original pre and post primitive input carriers from the actual callee recursion and argument construction. The real parameter reorder preserves the same assigned map. Complete basis trees and ordered ports, not equal widths, determine the retained input-code read of the primitive.
  • RuntimeNamedInputAction.original_input_action substitutes the complete authentic caller encoding into the same original parent Raw-event source-action law. The original child input proof and the checked selected ports derive its carrier and axis equalities. The independent sparse forest coefficients construct an arbitrary correlated spectator and reference fibre. No factorization of the joint state, supplied encoding equation or dense caller reconstruction is assumed. Native singleton code equality follows from the actual primitive reader. The equation retains the real final local reorder and the output code.
  • original_pre_post_input_actions applies these input laws to the pre and post event lists of the same original root, under the literal coverage and slice start and length premises. It does not infer those premises from matching widths.
  • The input-action laws do not transport the output fibre to the complete caller output encoding or source order. They do not compose the logical action or the observing history of the whole function. They are mathematical laws. They are not an additional native acceptance gate, a bounded availability claim or a guarantee admission. They change no executable kernel or Rust rule, effect label, work limit or public capability.
  • RuntimeNamedPrimitiveOutputs.original_pre_post_outputs derives the native output carriers through each real callee run, its original return reorder and the actual caller owner mapping. It retains complete basis trees and ports.
  • actual_occurrence_output_code attaches that same native code computation to the returned caller binding in its complete checked frame.
  • The interval-state identity lemmas compare successful reads of the same original block, start and count. Their derived empty checkpoints are erased proofs. They are not fabricated runtime receipts or extra work for the nonempty interval.
  • RuntimeNamedOutputEncoding.complete_output_encoding factors the complete caller output encoding through that native code. It retains arbitrary correlated spectator and reference coefficients.
  • Its original_pre_post_output_encodings consumer derives the target, the retained owner code and the native code read from each actual original call and its complete output frame. None is an assumed encoding equation.
  • RuntimeNamedOutputOrder transports dense logical coefficients by the exact cardinalities of the original owners, including padding and dimension-one owners. Its separate code identity requires equality of full ordered source-owner and wire pairs and the actual Raw frame. Code equality does not establish those source premises.
  • RuntimeNamedHeadCoefficients identifies the actual source input fibre and updates its exact logical coefficients with the true input and output cardinalities.
  • RuntimeNamedCallerGeometry derives the returned basis, the wires, the full Raw frame and the unchanged spectator bindings from the actual callee and caller boundary.
  • RuntimeNamedCallerAction.actual_whole_caller_action combines those facts with the same native output-code read. It proves the exact action on the complete returned caller encoding, for arbitrary correlated logical and reference states. It removes the final self-reorder only on actual finite physical rows. No unbounded identity of that event is assumed.
  • original_pre_post_actions instantiates both laws with the real child executions and exactly the event lists that the original root decomposition retains. The supplied complete checked frames are explicit premises. The theorem does not prove their construction for every source body.

The middle call:

  • RuntimeNamedSelectionInputs.original_middle_source derives the complete original input carriers of the middle selection from the real argument construction and child run. The strengthened common-loop invariant retains its exact before binding map and full returned source state. The actual final written return, including its reorder, starts at that selection after-map. All nominal trees, ports, spectators and separate zero-width owners stay in those maps. The theorem supplies source-state provenance. It supplies no caller coefficient or action equation and no proof of arbitrary intermediate frame availability.
  • RuntimeNamedSelectionFrames.original_middle_frames derives both mathematical child Frames from the complete caller input Frame. It selects the actual ordered argument owners and transports their existing receipts by full port and basis equality. It uses the original owner flow of the same selection for its after Frame. No final child Frame, successful readFrame invocation or bound on unspent work is supplied or fabricated.
  • RuntimeNamedBlockEncoding partitions the actual complete caller code into its original selected owners and retained spectators. It derives selected-token uniqueness from the real call input gate, including empty-wire owners, and does not infer it from physical axes. Exact owner cardinalities reindex the arbitrary joint and reference coefficients. No separability premise is introduced.
  • RuntimeNamedCarrierEncoding connects the actual input code of the retained child to those selected coefficients, by full ordered port and basis equality and the real Raw frame.
  • RuntimeNamedBlockSpectators derives disjoint axes from the complete valid caller. It proves that scattering selected axes leaves every spectator coefficient unchanged.
  • RuntimeNamedSelectionInputEncoding.actual_occurrence_source_action combines those facts with the same original child run, indexed Literal, coverage and parent-event source law. The source carrier equality is derived from that run, not supplied by a caller.
  • Its original_three_input_actions consumer retains all three complete-input action laws on the same original root event lists.
  • The selection output proof uses the actual return permutation of the child and the original mapping to caller owners. It transports the corresponding sparse coefficients through the exact output axes and applies each source arm on every spectator coordinate of the joint input. This yields the complete caller output in its original owner order, with all reference correlations.

Composition of the three calls and observation:

  • RuntimeNamedThreeFrameChain.original_three_composed takes its first frame from the original input storage and entry read. At both joins the same native state and source owner map carry the preceding output into the next call.
  • RuntimeNamedThreePackedOutput.original_three_packed also identifies the actual final Raw reorder and the owner reindex of the original return. Its finite-row equation includes the complete packed output for every joint logical input and reference coordinate.
  • RuntimeNamedThreePackedInstrument.original_three_observing connects that equation to the same independently read observing event list.
  • RuntimeObservingPrefix.checkOps_reference derives the same quantum interface in the independent reader after each successfully checked prefix. This includes erasure, reset and both sides of classical branches.
  • root_interval_histories uses that agreement to locate an adjacent pure interval in the original observing root. The interpreter preserves every inherited history. It applies the pure action to each operator before it continues with the original suffix and final reorder.
  • original_adjacent_observing locates the three original calls in a longer source traversal and retains the selection at its actual global rank. The same Raw events drive both the source-action equation and every inherited operator column that the checked input frame represents. The law requires that input representation, the supported call shapes and exact adjacency of their Raw slices. The packed root law uses explicit whole-slice coverage. The original-body theorem below uses the complete checked traversal. The law changes neither native acceptance nor the work limits.
  • RuntimeOriginalObservation.original_observation_histories covers a checked original measure_z or discard. It identifies the actual Raw erasure event and every emitted outcome. Each unnormalized operator on the surviving owner code is the basis effect of the original consumed owner on that outcome, with the same arbitrary reference coordinates. The theorem retains all hidden outcomes and the original visible measurement identifier. It requires the input code representation on finite Raw rows.
  • RuntimeNamedObservationEntry.original_supplies_histories transports every outcome into the entry frame of an original named call that follows immediately. It does so through the exact joins of the source state and of the Raw interval.
  • RawFiniteRows.checked_slice retains the finite input and output widths of the original checked event slices. Their action on each inherited history depends only on its finite input coefficients.
  • RuntimeNamedObservationEntry.original_erasure_then_adjacent ties the exact prefix, erasure, three-call interval and continuation to one original observing IR program. For each erasure outcome, the same three-call source equation acts on the unnormalized projected state in the checked post-call frame. It keeps the visible measurement and hidden outcome through all three calls. The equation applies to every finite post-call row and reference column of a represented incoming history.
  • When the post call ends both the original source traversal and the Raw operations, the actual suffix is the final permutation. The same theorem gives the packed source result in the original return order for every outcome. It identifies the list of histories that the original interpreter returns.

Branches and ordinary values:

  • RuntimeNamedChildRuns.original_body retains the actual input and output owner states for classical gaps and conditionals. For each conditional it keeps both original recursive arm reads and the successful join on their returned owner states and ordinary SSA tables, with the original work counters.
  • RuntimeOriginalBranch.original_branch_events identifies the exact Raw branch event, both arm traces and their final permutations. On a history whose ordinary values agree with the checked source expressions, original_branch_step selects the arm by the source condition.
  • RuntimeOriginalClassicalJoin.original_branch_classical_join uses the original Raw freshness check for every classical phi destination. Suppose that the selected arm returns histories with their checked SSA agreement and issued identities. The literal merge then produces one corresponding history per arm result, in order. Its visible values agree with the checked post-branch source expressions. Its quantum operator and hidden outcomes are those of that arm result.
  • RuntimeOriginalQuantumPhi.original_quantum_phi_action ties the actual arm-final Raw permutation to the complete original owner pairing. It retains the exact carrier layout of each owner, including separate zero-width owners, and derives the source output frame in its checked owner order. The equation holds for every finite output row and reference column. A represented arm history keeps its ordinary values and hidden outcomes through that exact permutation.
  • RuntimeOriginalBranchJoin.original_branch_join composes the source condition, the original arm run, its quantum return permutation and the literal classical merge. The original parent step returns one checked quantum and ordinary history for each actual arm-body result, in order.
  • RuntimeObservingValueRetention.run_values proves that each successful literal history retains all incoming values and only adds IDs from its trace.
  • RuntimeObservingPrefix.checkOps_reference_with_writes relates those writes, including recursive arm writes and phi destinations, to the issued IDs of the original check. The branch theorem derives this correspondence for every arm result from the support of the incoming history at the checked boundary.
  • checked_program_values obtains the same support for a complete original run from its own input bindings and native verification.
  • RuntimeOriginalOrdinaryGap.original_gap interprets the exact original classical interval with its checked SSA table. Each output is fresh in the actual Raw state. The independent run returns one history whose values agree with the resulting table. The history retains its operator and hidden outcomes.
  • RuntimeOriginalObservationValues.observation_agreement binds each actual measurement bit to the source measurement key that its checked call path transports. The valuation preserves every earlier successful expression, including the selected arm of a choose expression. Discard preserves the ordinary table. Both instructions preserve issued-ID support for the resulting history.
  • original_gap_values derives agreement in the valuation of the returned history itself. observation_step_values gives the same agreement for every history of the actual erasure event.

The complete original body:

  • RuntimeLiteralBody.original_body_recursive_refinement composes these laws for the complete staged original-body traversal. At each step the source operator follows the original primitive meaning, graph receipt, written transform or selection table. A written transform uses the exact logical matrix read from its checked forward body and the source-specified power, adjoint or control. Its ordered return replaces the selected owners and preserves the spectator bindings, including zero-width owners.
  • The same recursion follows actual named child reads and the arm that the checked ordinary condition selects. It applies the written return order to every result and relates the complete history lists in order. The statement starts with a successful checked body and a finite representation of the input operator. It retains the visible SSA agreement and hidden outcomes for each returned history. Validation of the full qmatch profile and release validation are separate from this theorem.
  • original_body_graph_refinement derives coherent selection coefficients from the original named arm graphs and checked inline bodies. For a mixed selection, each nominal selector ordinal is paired with its written arm in the actual checked table. An inline arm uses its own original source evaluation at a smaller runner depth, including its input encoding and literal Raw return order. The resulting coefficients give the same action as the corresponding sectors of the Raw program of the caller. The full result follows the source prefix and selected path, including named calls and ordinary branches.
  • native_qmatch_body_graph_refinement connects this theorem to successful Protocol.NativeContext.run .qmatchSourceV5 on the original packet. The same decision supplies the body and the compared execution view. The result preserves the complete ordered history family with List.Forall₂, the literal return order, visible SSA values and hidden outcomes.
  • native_qmatch_input_rows supplies the original row for every canonical ordinary input assignment.
  • These theorems have two explicit premises: the initial encoding relation between source and Raw, and a successful independent mathematical execution.

Not established by version 5

  • Validation of the full qmatch profile is open.
  • Release validation is separate.
  • Nonstructural qfor bodies are pending.
  • The duty checks do not close all general nested duties or establish source-action composition.
  • For arbitrary source bodies, the construction of caller frames and their availability are separate obligations.
  • The theorems do not prove native compilation, IO, Rust simulation or target preservation. They admit no guarantee.
  • Independent host-expression visibility and source/body preservation are separate obligations.
  • No external schema, inverse or control capability, guarantee admission or broader QS/PR/RS/EXACT discharge follows from this mode.

Root loading and compatibility during generic migration

This section states which sources a load checks, what provenance a receipt retains, and which compatibility duties a migration to generic rules keeps.

Rules for loading:

  • frontend::project::Project loads every .qli module beneath its selected source root and all bundled ordinary sources.
  • Ordinary project compilation checks the root of every materialized concrete ordinary function, including unused functions.
  • Classical bodies and Meaning declarations have their own obligations of preparation and checking, which are separate.
  • Common source checking covers every declaration, including unused declarations and both branch bodies.
  • QrateSource in src/frontend/project/manifest.rs provides opt-in selection of an explicitly declared [source].root. That selection chooses the source tree. It does not introduce reachable-only loading or exempt unused siblings inside the tree.
  • With an explicit module map, ParsedProgram::parse checks every supplied module and the bundled registry before it selects a concrete entry.

Rules for the provenance of receipts:

  • The function receipts and instrument receipts of the ordinary finite frontend retain source provenance separately from the loading policy. So do local equation sidecars.
  • Each retained declaration contributes its original resolved lexical dependencies, including type and Nat expressions, Meaning references, inactive branches and zero-count operations.
  • Actual bound Op descriptors and checked Raw receipt dependencies contribute their original source records as well.
  • Pure providers retain their original declaration and equation association. Instrument calls also retain the original caller and its concrete Op bindings for source-span binding.
  • The resulting closure retains complete original module text, including comments, and shares immutable module records across receipts. Unrelated loaded modules need not appear in each receipt.
  • The metadata limits and the aggregate native transport limits apply.
  • This selection changes neither loading nor eager checking of every loaded declaration. It does not implement a reachable-module policy.
  • These records provide provenance. They are not a source-preservation proof or acceptance authority.

Rules for a reachable-module policy, which this chapter does not enable:

  • Such a policy must specify entry roots, transitive imports, providers and Meaning dependencies, independent checking of the selected graph, bundled-library validation and the treatment of unused sources.
  • It must retain original module, root and dependency identities and reject stale, missing or replaced references.
  • It must preserve the permitted import-only cycles. Imports have no runtime action.
  • Forbidden dependency cycles through calls, Meanings and providers retain the rules of their actual profiles, including any explicitly admitted decreasing recursion.
  • Diagnostics and source-selection migration need review before a change of the all-source behavior.

Rules for compatibility:

  • The five-role architecture assigns compatibility duties for these: flat Raw IR, both QIRF profiles, finite contracts, five hierarchy modes, component protocols, the source, qrate and module-map entrypoints, the Rust and Python clients, foreign adapters and research comparisons.
  • The five hierarchy modes are --hierarchy-pending, --hierarchy-request-pending, --hierarchy-fourier-pending, --instrument-pending and --qpe-instrument-pending. The architecture records no compatibility duty for the sixth, --hierarchy-control-pending.
  • A later migration must preserve each supported contract, or state its explicit versioned replacement, its unsupported cases and its migration tests.
  • Replaced wrappers and their proofs must stay built and audited until their supported callers and obligations migrate.
  • Missing or incompatible native checking must reject through every route.
  • Compatibility does not promise to resurrect a retired API. frontend::sized moved to frontend::compile. The qleisli sized command prefix was removed, with explicit migration diagnostics.
  • The separate research and Python comparison readers do not restore that production namespace or supply alternative source acceptance.
  • Edition 2026 identifies the constitutional regime. Source, API and protocol compatibility is versioned separately.

Status and limits

Publication and proof are separate

  • Five things are distinct evidence: the unification of the implementation, publication, the compilation of proofs, tests and audits.
  • All of S05-C1–C5 are open. Full Soundness of the supported profile is targeted at version 0.5.0.
  • Neither this inventory nor an existing helper theorem automatically discharges a guarantee in the constitutional ledger.
  • Two scoped guarantees are admitted: QS-QLV1-OWNERSHIP-2026-01 for ownership and QS-QLV1-SCOPE-2026-01 for classical scope. Both concern the original decoded ordinary root. The broader obligations of the interpretations QS-2026-01, PR-2026-01, RS-2026-01 and EXACT-2026-01 are pending. No theorem that this chapter cites admits another guarantee.
  • Edition 2026 identifies the constitutional regime, independently of release and syntax compatibility.
  • The native executable, its transport, its decoder and the execution correspondence are explicit assumptions. Having Lean source does not prove compilation or the entire pipeline correct.

Shared exact-work ceiling

  • Ordinary and source-qmatch checks share a public ceiling of 20,000,000 exact-work units per request. The limit is inclusive.
  • Decoding, source and graph checks, and execution-view comparison spend from the same counter.
  • Rust also charges native receipts against the unspent exact work of the compilation, across all sites and calls.

CLI success reports

A successful check prints a report. This section states what the fields of that report claim and what they do not claim.

Without an explicit --entry, qleisli check <source-root> and qleisli check <directory> --qrate use the project route. They check the source project and its concrete lowered roots.

  • A successful native decision without a request establishes the applicable checks of IR structure, ownership, interface and classical scope. It does not establish an independently requested algorithm, the full meaning of the source, or preservation from source to IR.
  • The text success report names this scope and the actual canonical checker paths. It states whether independent requests were checked, and it states that source preservation is not proved.
  • The JSON report is the version-1 result envelope with outcome: "ok". Its diagnostics array holds only warnings and may be empty.

The result of a whole-project source check has these fields:

FieldMeaning
checker_pathsThe distinct canonical paths of the executables. The report captures them from the actual successful native invocations and does not resolve them again after checking. Several paths can occur if a selected symlink changes between invocations.
checker_identity"unpinned": the executable was selected and invoked, but its bytes were not checked against a trusted binary identity. A canonical path is not attestation.
native_decisions.countNumber of successful native acceptance decisions observed during this source check, including repeated decisions and decisions for partial source contracts.
native_decisions.requests_checkedNumber of those decisions with a separate native request payload checked by Lean. This counts decisions, not distinct source declarations or whole-source meanings.
native_decisions.completeWhether the metadata covers every successful decision and its checker path. If false, the bounded report is incomplete and its path list or counts must not be treated as exhaustive.
entry.presentWhether the ordinary project has a supported main::main entry. A library without that entry can check successfully.
entry.request_checkedWhether that entry’s own accepted artifact has a separately checked native request payload; null when there is no entry. Producer-generated typed requests count here without establishing an independent algorithm specification. Requests on other roots or partial contracts do not change this value.
entry.ordinary_result_checkedWhether this entry retains the native ordinary-v2 check of input and result over all hidden histories. False for absent entries and other modes.
entry.runtime_result_checkedWhether this entry retains the native finite-runtime-root-v2 check of complete type and storage, quantum code space and all hidden histories. True also for a version-5 decision, whose request carries the runtime-root request. False for absent entries and other modes.
entry.source_body_scopeOptional. Present only when the entry retains a version-5 decision. Its value is the checked profile name, such as finite-source-qmatch-context-v5. The text report prints it on the line entry source body checked:.
concrete_ir_roots.local, concrete_ir_roots.bundledCounts of the checked roots of concrete ordinary functions. The two fields separate loaded project and dependency modules from bundled library modules.
source_preservation_verifiedfalse: this command does not prove source-to-IR preservation.

Rules for reading the counts:

  • All loaded bundled concrete functions are checked, including unused ones. Their decisions and roots therefore contribute to the report.
  • Generic operation expansions occur within enclosing concrete roots. A registered specialization is not an additional root.
  • Constructing or declaring an unused Meaning does not imply that Lean checked a corresponding equation.
  • Pure, function and instrument contract requests have their individual native scopes. When they are separate external requests, their successful decisions contribute to requests_checked. They assert no whole-entry Meaning or general source preservation. A positive aggregate request count can accompany entry.request_checked: false.
  • The request fields describe the separate external request payload, not Meaning entries embedded in an ordinary QIRF artifact. A zero request count does not claim that no embedded Meaning was checked.
  • A reachable FunctionEvidence dependency is checked with its ordinary QIRF root. That invocation contributes to the decision count and has no separate request payload. Reading the counters does not identify or prove its exact dependency equation.
  • Request data can itself be producer generated. Checking it does not establish an independent specification of the original source.

Reports of the other commands:

  • On the selected-entry route, check --entry ... reports four fields beside its verification scope and request_origin: the singular actual checker_path of the selected root, checker_identity: "unpinned", request_checked and source_preservation_verified: false. These fields describe the receipt of the selected root. They are not an aggregate of every native decision made while preparing and checking the source.
  • The native-validity scope of the Raw route is distinct from the hierarchy composition, Fourier, instrument and named-QPE request scopes.
  • Finite artifact reports also expose ordinary_result_checked and runtime_result_checked, with the meanings of the project-entry fields. They expose the optional source_body_scope in the same way, and the text report prints it on the line source body checked:.
  • request_checked: true also applies to a checked producer-consistency request. It does not assert an independent specification of the Meaning of the source. source_meaning_verified: false stays explicit.
  • verify-ir reports the singular actual checker_path of the checked artifact, checker_identity: "unpinned" and request_checked. With --against, the request result applies to that exact supplied pair of artifact and request.
  • emit-ir reports its output path with the checker and request metadata of the emitted root.
  • The text successes of verify-ir and emit-ir state the IR and request scope. Success of neither command establishes preservation from a source, a trusted binary identity, or correctness of downstream execution or export.
  • interop check uses the same singular actual-root metadata in its JSON success. Importing foreign source and accepting its lowered artifact do not prove translation preservation.
  • Request-free success is a successful structural check. No independent Meaning is inferred from it.
  • The report fields alter no acceptance rule, proof scope or admitted constitutional guarantee.

Public operations that confer no acceptance

The public operations in this table confer no acceptance. The second column states what each operation does instead.

OperationScope
RawProgram, RawOp, native::Proposal::{new,from_raw}Untrusted IR or serialized proposals. Structural validity does not imply native acceptance. The 22 coverage entries of the RawOp constructors describe checking coverage. They do not describe constructor authority.
Circuit::new, Encoding::{new,identity}, Contract::new, FiniteMeaning::{permutation,phase,matrix,target_ir}, UnitaryBoundary::new, matrix codecsDescriptions, exact arithmetic and bounded host construction. A proposed meaning is not evidence that an implementation has that meaning.
qleisli doc → render_markdownReads and parses documentation, and returns before source compilation. It confers no type or semantic acceptance.
Source loading, edition configuration and Kernel::newConfigure files or a checker path. Later checking can fail.
Checked-object accessors and check_binding / check_entryRetain or compare the original checked identity and scope. They do not make a fresh decision of semantic acceptance.
Foreign exportConsumes AcceptedProgram and emits target text. The terminal OpenQASM adapter can project a closed typed source result to its ordered measured bits, or emit no bits for Unit. Input acceptance does not prove preservation of the emitted OpenQASM/QIR or target execution. QIRF export separately performs a fresh native validity check on its output. Output validity alone is not a translation theorem.
sim, host, hierarchy execution and samplingExecute already checked descriptions numerically. Acceptance and bounded reference tests do not establish runtime or floating-point preservation.

Rules for the H; Z; H replacement in OpenQASM/QIR export:

  • Export may replace three adjacent actual expanded function steps, H; Z; H, with the existing X/CX/CCX word. The target axis and the ordered zero, one or two controls, including polarity, must match in all three steps. Z must have identity permutation and exact eighth-turn phases [0,4].
  • No source name or inferred label authorizes this replacement, and no step commutes across another. Nonmatching words keep the emitter policy. The original accepted graph, source types, owners and dependencies stay intact.
  • A final target-word pass also recognizes exactly adjacent uncontrolled H; Z; H on one identical physical operand, including words separated by pure Raw operation boundaries. It reads the actual emitted gate definitions and operand maps. It uses the same native equation gate, receipt cache and export-wide work counter.
  • Allocation, singleton preparation, measurement and discard boundaries prevent a window from crossing them. No phase folding, commuting or source-name lookup creates a window.
  • The final pass starts only after the gate stream from cursor normalization and lowering has satisfied the 4,096-gate cap. Final shortening cannot admit an otherwise over-limit emitted stream. Other target limits and original checked obligations are unchanged.
  • Each distinct compact pair of original and replacement Raw requires the native function-equation check under the checker of the input AcceptedProgram. The local comparison retains full scalar phase and ordered control polarities.
  • An export retains at most seven complete-body local receipts. It shares the 20,000,000 exact-work budget across all Raw operations.
  • Unavailable checking, rejection or exhausted capacity produces no artifact and no alternate acceptance path.
  • This bounded local comparison is not a general preservation theorem for source, target emission, physical resources or external QIS. The local equations do not establish general source/export, resource or external QIS preservation. The two adopted guarantees and the pending QS/PR/RS/EXACT obligations keep their scopes.

Rules for explicit module-map source selection:

  • Explicit module-map source selection parses, instantiates, elaborates and lowers untrusted proposals. Ordinary commands with explicit entry and module bindings use the shared source execution plan.
  • emit-proposal checks source contracts and operation Meaning requests with the selected kernel before writing the transport. It reports untrusted-proposal.
  • The preselected Raw route uses ordinary native acceptance. It then separately compares the accepted instructions with the retained source steps.
  • The hierarchy route retains dedicated request, Fourier, instrument or named-QPE checking and the required initialization-move binding.
  • A native failure cannot switch routes or discard the request of the caller.
  • Selected checking and execution results retain source_meaning_verified: false. Native validity, producer consistency, caller composition and named-QPE requests have distinct scopes.
  • Neither source-step comparison nor general lowering preservation follows merely from an accepted proposal. Selected-source execution states the other invocation and checking-profile boundaries.

Rules for the Isometry profile of the hierarchy route:

  • A source root with a checked public Isometry contract and an actual Unitary or Isometry body uses the supported Isometry profile through the check_instrument_native boundary. The profile has fresh-zero preparation, checked unitary evolution and a readout with zero measurements. A unitary body needs no preparation step.
  • This transport selection preserves the public bound. It does not rewrite the actual source-step or Raw effect to Isometry.
  • The quantum entry and result trees, zero-width owners and the complete live frame are part of the proposal and its initialization-move comparison.
  • At most one ordinary Bits<0> result may accompany the quantum results. The empty outcome of the transport does not create a source Observe effect.
  • Isometry execution returns its single unnormalized branch with scalar phase retained.
  • Sampling requires a checked public Observe contract and an actually observing supported artifact.
  • Conservative public bounds cannot recover sharper source eligibility or fabricate actual operations. The Raw profile keeps its actual classification and explicit support limits. A public Observe contract over a pure body is outside this hierarchy profile.
  • This adapter reuses component checks. It introduces no native primitive, accepted-handle authority, formal theorem or constitutional guarantee. The ordinary QLV1 ownership and scope admissions do not extend to this hierarchy path.
  • An independent hierarchy request must fit the supported composition language. A whole-root finite-matrix request cannot replace the required child structure of a composite root.
  • Producer consistency, the bounded initialization and source-step comparison and numerical execution observations keep their separate scopes. General source preservation and the complete native analytic/operator and runtime correspondence duties are pending.

Numerical result presentation

This section covers how run presents numerical results, and the optional annotation of exact zeros.

  • Closed-project run reports a numerical reference distribution. Text uses scientific notation with twelve digits after the decimal point. JSON retains numeric probabilities under the output range policy.
  • Reset and discard trace out the last quantum axis by summing both hidden outcome weights. Visible measurements retain every numerically positive outcome, including rare events and floating-point residues. These rows count toward the ensemble limits.
  • Sampling uses the numerical execution model. A small floating-point residue can appear at a mathematically zero outcome.
  • For project-mode text run, --show-exact-zeros appends [exact zero] to a displayed row when a bounded calculation finds its exact amplitude equal to zero. Each numerical value and output word stays in the original order. The formatter uses no probability threshold and leaves unlisted rows absent. The option is exclusive to project-mode text run.
  • The calculation uses the retained Raw of a closed, already accepted program. The profile permits vacuum preparation, structural register and Unit operations, injective LiftBasis, exact Hadamard and monomial steps, and sealed coherent selection with its full phase.
  • Each LiftBasis appends fresh zero axes and uses the actual table in declared axis order. Terminal Z measurement reads each axis once, and the result contains each measured bit once.
  • A program outside this profile, or an exhausted resource or arithmetic limit, prints the numeric distribution and reports why the exact annotation is unavailable. Default text, JSON and seeded sampling keep their numerical behavior.
  • The annotation is presentation evidence within this bounded Raw profile. The native checker is the authority for exact contracts and accepted handles.
Limit of the exact annotationValue
Allocated axesSix
Raw operations2,048
Expanded steps1,024
Exact evaluation budgetOne million units, separate, with the finite dyadic complex arithmetic used for circuit proposals

Coverage checks

A coverage record holds the inventory of this boundary, and a script checks the repository against it.

  • tests/fixtures/verification_v029/coverage.json.xz separates four things: current implementation, published 0.2.9 validation, unpublished development and open proof obligations. It records the current coverage groups, boundary entry lists, constructor variants and classified paths.
  • Engineering comparisons and the check-only nominal carrier component have distinct classifications. Mixed boundary rows refer to individually classified paths. A public surface that contains a constructor or doc is not counted wholesale as native acceptance.
  • scripts/check_production_coverage.py checks five things: the reviewed public surface, complete path classifications, all native modes and dispatch targets, named source and declaration bindings and existing regression functions.
  • The script fails on an omitted route, an exposed boundary that the inventory lacks, changed dispatch, a missing binding or a proposal misclassified as acceptance. The native-contract proof scope also retains the explicit encoded-equation and guarantee-admission limits.
  • These checks detect inventory drift. Source markers and test existence are not formal proof or evidence that a test has just run. The underlying inventories, actual tests, proof builds and audits are necessary.
  • Existing regression bindings include tests/native_paths.rs, tests/function_evidence.rs, tests/semantic_contracts.rs, tests/finite_leaf.rs, scripts/test_source_kernel.py, scripts/test_interop_native.py, tests/hierarchical_host.rs, tests/hierarchical_qpe_host.rs, tests/sized_source.rs, and the explicit no-kernel proposal test in tests/sized_cli.rs. The separate doc regression is in tests/cli.rs.
  • Their bounded observations do not replace S05 proofs or human review of the intended semantics.
